chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The ritual bath (ghusl) on Friday is obligatory for men and women when at home (in residence), and for men when travelling.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for Friday bath for men and women during travel and residence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the scope of the obligatory Friday ritual bath (ghusl al-Jumu'ah), distinguishing between the obligations for men and women in settled communities versus the specific requirement for men during travel. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction highlights the communal nature of the Friday prayer for men, while acknowledging the varying degrees of obligation for women who may not always attend the congregational prayer. The ruling underscores the importance of physical and spiritual preparation for the weekly gathering, reflecting the holistic approach to worship in the Imami tradition.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Both men and women should take a shower/bath on Friday when at home.  If travelling, men should take a shower’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Both men and women should take a shower on Friday when at home. On the journey men should take a shower on Friday.’”
